To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) session-based DCG, normalized session-based DCG and estimated session nDCGs have reasonable but weak correlation with the user experience measures; and (2) the first and the worst query's nDCGs in a session have strong correlation with the user measures.

nsDCG and estimated session nDCGs (esNDCGs) have reasonable correlations with users' self-ratings on search performance and task difficulties; and the worst query's nDCGs and the last query’s nDCGs in a session have comparable correlations with these user metrics.
session-based DCG metrics are not good predictors of users' search experience, but query-based metrics are.
